Which schools serve Wayne neighborhoods?

Wayne Public Schools teach pre-kindergarten through grade 12 in 15 schools, with 7,746 students enrolled in the 2022-23 school year. Wayne Hills High School serves students who live on or north of Ratzer Road, and Wayne Valley High School serves those south of it, so your street decides your high school. Elementary schools include Dey, Fallon, Kennedy, Lafayette, Packanack, Pines Lake, Ryerson, Terhune and Carter, and the three middle schools are Schuyler-Colfax, George Washington and Anthony Wayne.

Passaic County Technical Institute also admits students from across the county. Private options include DePaul Catholic High School and Al-Ghazaly High School.

What is a Continued Certificate of Occupancy in Wayne?

Wayne requires a CCO for the sale or rental of one- and two-family homes, duplexes, townhouses and condominiums. No residential premises may change ownership, tenancy or use without a CCO from the Enforcement Officer under Township Code Section 100. A transfer between spouses, from parent to child, or between siblings does not need one.

  • Apply and pay the base fee online. The Building Department then checks for open permits, and open permits must be closed before an inspection is scheduled.
  • After that, the enforcement officer has 15 business days to inspect and either issue the certificate or list the failed items.
  • Inspections sooner than 10 days after the application and permit closure carry an expediting fee.
  • A CCO is valid for 90 days. If closing slips past that, you must reapply.

The inspection checks the house against the zoning and property maintenance ordinances, including any addition, finished basement, shed, second kitchen, deck or pool, and each must have a permit or a variance. If the house fails or permits are still open, the township may allow the sale to close on a signed purchaser's agreement that names who will fix the items. That agreement cannot run longer than 60 days, and the buyer schedules the follow-up inspection.

A separate CCO fire inspection is also needed. Call the CCO Office at 973-694-1800, extension 3263, and the Fire Bureau at extension 3300. The township's CCO page links a search for open permits, so check it before you apply.

On the state chart for prices above $350,000, the slice from $550,000 to $850,000 costs $5.30 per $500 and the slice to $1,000,000 costs $5.80. Anything higher adds a Graduated Percent Fee that begins at 1%. Every owner files a GIT/REP form with the deed.

A New Jersey resident files GIT/REP-3. Sellers who have moved out of state file GIT/REP-1 or 2 and may prepay 2% of the price or 8.97% of the gain. The township has also warned residents about a phone scam claiming a property is in a tax sale. To confirm what you owe, call the township at 973-694-1800, extension 3330, and do not send money to a caller.

How do Wayne assessments and appeals work?

Passaic County keeps the usual calendar. Appeals are due April 1, moving to May 1 after a revaluation or reassessment. Form A-1 goes to the Passaic County Board of Taxation in Totowa (930 Riverview Drive, Suite 250; 973-720-7399). Assessments above $1,000,000 may go to the Tax Court.

The burden of proof is yours, so bring recent sales of comparable homes. Sellers rarely benefit from an appeal, but an heir or buyer keeping the house might.

What are the quick-sale choices in Wayne?

  • Agent listing: broad exposure to commuters and university-area buyers, with weeks of showings and lender timelines.
  • Private sale: saves a commission, and you handle the CCO, disclosures and contracts.
  • Cash offer: no mortgage contingency, and a buyer willing to close on a purchaser's agreement if an item fails.

Whatever you choose, start the CCO early and find open permits first, since that clock controls most Wayne closing dates.

How long does a Wayne CCO take?

The enforcement officer has 15 business days to inspect and decide once the permit check is clear. Expedited inspections inside 10 days carry an extra fee, so apply as early as you can.

Is a CCO required when I give my house to a family member?

No for transfers between spouses, from parent to child, or between siblings. Other transfers of one- or two-family homes need the Continued Certificate of Occupancy.

How long does a Wayne CCO last?

Ninety days from issue. If closing has not happened by then, the certificate expires and a new application is needed.

When is the deadline to appeal a property tax assessment in Wayne?

April 1, unless the township did a revaluation or reassessment, in which case it is May 1. File with the Passaic County Board of Taxation in Totowa at 973-720-7399.

Can I sell my Wayne house if it fails the CCO inspection?

Possibly. The township may allow closing on a purchaser's agreement that says who corrects the items, for no more than 60 days, and the buyer schedules the follow-up inspection.

West Milford is a sprawling, lake-dotted township in northern Passaic County, and a sale here turns on three things: a fire-safety certificate from the township, the assessment calendar kept by the Passaic County Board of Taxation, and a deed filed with the county clerk in Paterson. At 75.93 square miles of land, West Milford is the biggest municipality in Passaic County and holds over 40 percent of the county's area. The Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate is 25,216 residents, about 327 per square mile, and workers face a commute near 40 minutes.

How did West Milford's history and land shape its homes?

The legislature formed the township in 1834 out of the western half of Pompton Township. Its name comes from a post office mix-up: a clerk in Washington is said to have given the label West Milford to the western of two places called New Milford. Trains once brought summer visitors to stations at Charlotteburg, Newfoundland, Oak Ridge, Hewitt and Awosting, and steamboats crossed Greenwood Lake to the resorts. After the war the cottages around the lakes gradually became year-round houses.

Today the township describes itself as many small towns, with the township center, Hewitt, Newfoundland and Oak Ridge as the four main communities. Greenwood Lake runs about nine miles and crosses into New York, and smaller waters such as Upper Greenwood Lake, Wonder Lake and Lake Lockover have their own clusters of homes.

The local district, West Milford Township Public Schools, covers pre-K through grade 12 with elementary schools, Macopin Middle School and West Milford High School. It enrolled 3,028 students in 2021-22, and Westbrook Elementary closed before the 2023-24 year. Passaic County Technical Institute accepts selected students from across the county. Families will want the elementary school for your street named in the listing, so get that from the district office.

What certificate does West Milford require before a house is sold?

A house for one or two households cannot change owners until the Fire Marshal's office certifies that its smoke and CO alarms pass inspection. The state rule is N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3, and skipping it can mean a fine of up to $2,500. Inspections are booked for Wednesdays, so start early.

  • Fees on the township's February 2025 sheet run $55 for a request made more than 10 business days ahead, $100 for four to ten days, and $165 inside four business days. A second visit costs $50.
  • Alarms must carry a UL listing and be under 10 years old, and plain battery units must use sealed 10-year batteries.
  • Any home with a fuel-burning appliance, fireplace, wood stove or attached garage needs a CO alarm.
  • No certificate is issued unless house numbers at least four inches tall can be seen from the street.
  • A solar array, generator or battery backup calls for a label by the electric panel and meter that reads "CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER."
  • The fire extinguisher requirement for one- and two-family homes ended February 3, 2025.

The certificate lasts six months and does not transfer to a later owner. The Fire Prevention Bureau is at 13 Edgar Drive, and its phone is 973-728-2840.

How do West Milford tax assessments and appeals work?

The assessor mails a postcard to every owner on February 1 listing the assessment for the current tax year. If you think it is too high, a petition goes to the Passaic County Board of Taxation by April 1, and forms are available from the township assessor at 973-728-2793. Added or omitted assessments, which appear when new construction is added to the roll partway through a year, have a separate December 1 deadline.

The county board sits at 930 Riverview Drive, Suite 250, in Totowa, and its 2026 regular deadline was April 1, 2026. When you sell, ask the township tax collector for your current balance and any sewer charge so the title company can build an exact payoff.

Where is a West Milford deed filed, and what does the seller pay the state?

The Passaic County Clerk's Registry Division, at 401 Grand Street, Room 113, in Paterson, records West Milford deeds. A deed must show a "Prepared by" line, the tax block and lot, the price and a return address. The office asks for an official cover sheet, and without one it adds $20 per document.

The seller also pays the state realty transfer fee, a tiered charge that rises with the price and is paid by trust account check. Your closing attorney will compute it from the state schedule, and the county adds a $5 homelessness trust fund charge per document.

Which sale route fits a West Milford house?

The lakes, long drives and low turnover here affect which route makes sense, and each one still needs the alarm certificate and a clean title.

  • An agent listing helps most when the house is far from Route 23 or on a lake road, because the wide buyer pool includes commuters who will trade drive time for space.
  • A sale on your own can work with a neighbor or relative as buyer, though you take on pricing, disclosures and the contract.
  • A cash purchase suits an inherited house, a camp-style cottage needing work or an owner who has already moved away.

Compare offers by the amount left after the certificate, taxes, state fee and repairs, not by the headline price.

Frequently asked questions

Is an alarm certificate required to sell in West Milford?

Yes, for houses of one or two units. The Fire Marshal's office issues it, the township sheet lists fees of $55, $100 or $165 depending on how near closing you apply, and it expires after six months.

Can I sell a West Milford house that needs major repairs?

Yes. The alarm certificate looks at alarms, house numbers and a few related items, not the overall condition of the house. A mortgage lender may still demand repairs, while a cash buyer can take it in its current condition.

By what date must a West Milford assessment appeal be filed?

Every April 1, with the Passaic County Board of Taxation, once the February postcard has arrived. Appeals about added or omitted assessments are due December 1.

Which office records a West Milford deed?

The Passaic County Clerk's Registry Division in Paterson. The closing attorney or title agent files it and sends the seller's transfer fee at the same time.

Does the Highlands Act affect a West Milford sale?

It can shape what a buyer may build. West Milford lies in the Highlands preservation area, so additions and new lots face added state rules, while an existing house sells like any other.

What are the routes to a closing for a Bernards Township house?

A Bernards Township owner can put the house on the market, sell it to a buyer found privately, or accept a cash bid for the property as it stands. The township layers its own pre-sale steps over state rules, so the actual pace depends on how quickly permits and inspections get cleared.

With homes valued around $814,800 at the median, many buyers finance, and a listing draws them. A cash bid answers different problems: an inherited house in Basking Ridge, a property whose permits were never closed, a rental after the tenant leaves, or a seller who needs a date that will hold.

  • Private sale: no agent fee, with pricing, marketing and township paperwork on your desk.

How do the Census numbers describe Bernards Township homeowners?

Housing values here sit far above the national median of $332,700. The Census Bureau puts the township at 28,594 residents in July 2025. Owners live in 83.1 percent of the housing units. Households bring in $194,107 at the median and $109,797 per person, and rent at the median is $2,476.

Adults here are highly educated, with 74.2 percent holding a bachelor's degree or higher. Foreign-born residents are 25.3 percent of the population, and 24.1 percent of people are under 18. A language other than English is spoken at home by 29.4 percent of those age 5 and up. Monthly owner costs reach the top bracket the survey reports: $4,000 or more with a mortgage, $1,500 or more without one.

At these price levels buyers expect a clean permit file, and the township checks for one before any residential sale anyway.

Where is Bernards Township and what is it made of?

Bernards sits at the eastern end of the Somerset Hills and covers 24.33 square miles, nearly all of it land. The Second Watchung Mountain bounds the southwest, the Dead River swamp lies to the south, and the Great Swamp National Wildlife Refuge, the Passaic River and Millington Gorge form the eastern edge. Within the township are Basking Ridge, Liberty Corner, Lyons, Franklin Corners, Mount Horeb, Madisonville and part of The Hills, and the Martinsville ZIP Code 08836 covers a piece of it too.

The area was chartered in 1760 as Bernardston Township and incorporated as Bernards Township on February 21, 1798. Far Hills split off in 1921 and Bernardsville in 1924. Voters turned down a borough of Basking Ridge by better than four to one. The township now has 138.86 miles of roads and neighbors Bedminster, Bernardsville, Bridgewater, Warren, Harding and Long Hill.

What must a Bernards Township seller obtain before closing?

Two things, both issued from 277 South Maple Avenue in Basking Ridge. The first is an inspection and certification of smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and a fire extinguisher from the Bureau of Fire Prevention. The second is a Construction Records Clearance from the Code Enforcement Division. The township's selling guide, revised June 2026, says to create a free account on its online portal to apply.

The clearance rule in the township code says a Construction Records Clearance is required before the sale of any residential structure, and both owner and purchaser can be held responsible if one is not issued. The inspector checks records for open construction or zoning permits, and any open permit must have its final inspection before the clearance issues. File at least 10 business days before the change of ownership. A violation carries a fine up to $1,000, up to 90 days in jail or up to 90 days of community service.

How are Bernards Township property taxes set and paid?

The Tax Collector posts a 2026 total rate of $1.661. Of that, $0.275 funds the county, $0.030 county open space, $1.077 the school district, $0.246 the municipality and $0.033 the library. Four installments fall on the first of February, May, August and November, and the 10th of each of those months is the last day of grace. Postmarks do not count; the payment must be physically in the office.

Collections reached 99.50 percent of the 2025 levy across 10,358 tax accounts and 7,231 sewer accounts counted on January 1, 2026. Sewer bills follow their own cycle, due January 1 and July 1 with a 30-day grace period. A closing in the middle of a quarter is prorated, so get a current balance on both the tax and sewer accounts.

Veteran and senior deductions exist. Seniors qualify at 65 or older on October 1 of the prior year, if they live in the home and stay under the income limit; tell your attorney if a deduction is in place.

Do floods affect a sale in Bernards Township?

They can. The Passaic River runs along the township's edge, and the township keeps a flood information page with flood zone maps for buildings, floodways, open space and township property. It also lists its National Flood Insurance Program Class 7 approval and links to FEMA maps and elevation guides.

Ask a buyer's lender whether the property needs flood insurance, and look up the parcel on the township and FEMA maps before you list. A seller who can show an elevation certificate or a clear zone designation answers a common buyer question in the first week.

What do transit, roads and schools add to Bernards Township listings?

Interstate 78, Interstate 287 and U.S. Route 202 serve the township. NJ Transit's Gladstone Branch stops at Basking Ridge and Lyons stations on the way to Hoboken Terminal, and Lakeland Bus Lines runs a Route 78 rush-hour service from Bedminster to the Port Authority Bus Terminal. Mean travel time to work is 32.5 minutes.

The Bernards Township School District runs six schools, among them Cedar Hill, Liberty Corner, Mount Prospect and Oak Street elementary schools, William Annin Middle School and Ridge High School. Ridge High School won a National Blue Ribbon award in 2009 to 2010. The district reported 4,874 students in 2020 to 2021. Private options include Pingry School's upper campus in Basking Ridge and Saint James School.

What changes when a Bernards Township buyer pays cash?

Paying cash takes out the lender's appraisal and most repair haggling. The Construction Records Clearance, the Bureau of Fire Prevention certification and the state transfer fee all stay in place. Agree up front who files each application, because the clearance fee climbs as closing nears.

Weigh offers by what you keep. A listing may fetch more, but commission, staging, inspection credits and holding costs come out of it. Above $1,000,000 the buyer owes an extra 1 percent fee beyond the seller's own transfer fee.

Frequently asked questions

Is a smoke detector certificate the only thing Bernards Township asks for?

No. The Code Enforcement Division also issues a Construction Records Clearance before a residential sale. Its review looks for open construction or zoning permits, which need final inspections before the clearance is released.

How much does a Construction Records Clearance cost in Bernards Township?

$40 if it reaches the township more than 10 calendar days ahead of closing, $75 inside 10 days and $125 inside 4 days. The township asks for the application at least 10 business days before ownership changes.

When are Bernards Township property taxes due?

The first of February, May, August and November, with grace through the 10th. The money must be in the Tax Collector's hands by then, since a postmark proves nothing. Sewer bills are due January 1 and July 1.

Which transfers skip the Bernards clearance?

A transfer is exempt when occupancy stays the same. The code lists a deed correction, a transfer between spouses, an estate distribution by an executor or administrator, and refinancing or home equity loans.

Does the buyer ever pay a transfer fee in New Jersey?

Only when the price is above $1,000,000. The seller pays the standard realty transfer fee in every sale, and the buyer owes an added 1 percent when consideration exceeds that line.

What are the fastest ways to sell in Bridgewater Township?

An owner in a hurry can accept a cash offer, hire a listing agent, or find a buyer without one. In this township the listing route is strong, because prices are high and buyers are plentiful, so people pick cash for other reasons: a house in need of work, a relocation date, an estate, or a landlord leaving the business.

Bridgewater Township sits in the middle of Somerset County in the Raritan Valley, about 32 miles from Manhattan. The Census Bureau estimates 46,455 residents on July 1, 2025, up 1.0% from the 2020 base, which makes it the county's second-largest municipality after Franklin Township.

What does the Bridgewater housing market look like?

Bridgewater is among the pricier towns in central New Jersey. Census figures for 2020 to 2024 show a median owner-occupied value of $605,500, an owner-occupied rate of 84.9%, median household income of $172,851, and median gross rent of $2,176. About 16,505 households average 2.75 people, and 61.8% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree. Median owner costs with a mortgage run $3,258 a month, so buyers are sensitive to taxes and condition.

The township spreads over 31.89 land square miles and mixes older neighborhoods with large newer developments. It is split into recognized sections without formal borders:

  • Bradley Gardens, an older southwestern area with newer pockets and a commercial strip on Old York Road.
  • Green Knoll, the central area with Bridgewater Commons, the municipal building and the high school.
  • Finderne, in the southeast, with older streets, newer developments and TD Bank Ballpark, home to the Somerset Patriots.
  • Martinsville, the largest census-designated place at 12,147 residents in 2020, and Bridgewater Center in the west.

How do jobs, commuting and shopping affect Bridgewater buyers?

Bridgewater is the commercial hub of Somerset County. Pharmaceutical and life-science employers anchor the economy, with Sanofi's U.S. headquarters in the township, and Bridgewater Commons, a mall of roughly 994,000 square feet anchored by Bloomingdale's and Macy's, draws shoppers from several counties. The Census lists average travel time to work at 31.4 minutes, which fits a place where many residents commute out and many workers commute in.

Interstate 287 is the main limited-access road, Interstate 78 passes through the north without exits, and U.S. 22, Route 28 and Routes 202-206 cross the township. The Raritan Valley Line stops at Bridgewater station, and NJ Transit buses run to the Port Authority Bus Terminal (route 114) and Newark (route 65). Newark Liberty Airport is about 25 miles away. Buyers moving from New York or north Jersey often ask which streets are closest to the station and the highways, so put that in the listing.

Which schools serve Bridgewater homes?

Most of the township is in the Bridgewater-Raritan Regional School District, the largest in Somerset County, which also serves the borough of Raritan. It operated 11 schools and 8,254 students in 2020-21. The primary schools are Adamsville, Bradley Gardens, Crim, Hamilton, John F. Kennedy (in Raritan), Milltown and Van Holten; Eisenhower and Hillside are intermediate schools for grades 5 and 6; Bridgewater-Raritan Middle School covers grades 7 and 8; and Bridgewater-Raritan High School serves grades 9 through 12.

The township is also home to the Somerset County Vocational and Technical High School, a county magnet school, and the headquarters of the Somerset County Library System. Because buyers often shop by elementary zone, confirm the primary school for your street with the district before you advertise it.

What does Bridgewater require before you renovate or sell?

The township's Code Enforcement office administers construction permits and issues certificates of approval and occupancy after final inspection. A permit is generally needed for decks, pools, additions, garages, finishing a basement, new electrical outlets, and new or replacement furnaces, water heaters or air conditioning. A shed needs one if it is over 200 square feet or has utilities, a fence only if it is over 6 feet or serves as a pool barrier, and roofing only where sheathing is replaced. State law lets the construction official fine unpermitted work up to $2,000 per violation, which is why open or missing permits surface during a buyer's review. Plan review can take up to 20 working days.

Home fire safety requirements and applications are handled by the township's Fire Safety office. Call the main line at 908-725-6300, extension 5560 for construction questions and extension 5550 for fire safety, to confirm what a buyer's inspection will check. The municipal offices are at 100 Commons Way.

How are Bridgewater property taxes billed and appealed?

Bridgewater bills in four installments. The tax collector lists due dates of February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a ten-day grace period. If the lender escrows your taxes, the lender must supply the correct bank code to the tax office, and when a mortgage is paid off at closing the office should be told to remove it. The assessor runs an annual reassessment program, and each property must be inspected on a four-year cycle, so a visit from the township's appraisal contractor before a sale is not unusual.

What does the state charge on a higher-priced Bridgewater sale?

With a median value above $600,000, many Bridgewater sales exceed the thresholds in New Jersey's Realty Transfer Fee schedule. The seller pays at recording. For deals above $350,000 the rate per $500 of price runs $2.90 on the first $150,000, $4.25 up to $200,000, $4.80 up to $550,000 and $5.30 from $550,000 to $850,000.

When the price tops $1,000,000 for a residential property, a supplemental Graduated Percent Fee applies and the seller is responsible for it: 1% for sales up to $2,000,000, 2% up to $2,500,000, 2.5% up to $3,000,000, 3% up to $3,500,000 and 3.5% above that. The Division of Taxation posts the exemptions and forms, including RTF-1EE, on its realty transfer fee page. A cash buyer's lower price should be compared against these fees plus commission, not just the headline number.

What flood and site issues come up in Bridgewater?

The Raritan River forms much of the southern edge, and the North Branch of the Raritan marks the western border. In August 2011, Hurricane Irene submerged the former American Cyanamid Superfund site, about 560 acres of which lie in the township, and chemicals leaked into the river. If your home is low-lying near the river, ask the township engineering office about flood information before you list, and keep any flood insurance and repair records for the buyer. The northeastern part, by contrast, is hilly because the First Watchung Mountain runs through it.

February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, each with a ten-day grace period. A tenth day that lands on a weekend or holiday moves the cutoff to the next business day.

The township's assessor page lists May 1 of the tax year as the appeal due date. Confirm the date against the notice you receive from the Tax Assessor at 908-725-6300, extension 5121.

Does a Bridgewater shed or fence need a permit?

Only in some cases. A shed needs a permit if it is over 200 square feet or has electric or plumbing, and a fence needs one if it is over 6 feet tall or serves as a pool barrier.

Which school district covers Bridgewater?

The Bridgewater-Raritan Regional School District, which covers pre-kindergarten through grade 12 for Bridgewater and the borough of Raritan. The district reported 11 schools in the 2020-21 school year.

Does a sale above $1,000,000 cost more in New Jersey?

Yes. Residential sales above $1,000,000 carry a Graduated Percent Fee on top of the Realty Transfer Fee, starting at 1% of total consideration, and the seller is responsible for it.

What sets a Franklin Township, NJ house sale apart from nearby towns?

Franklin Township is a large Somerset County township, and unlike Garfield or Freehold Township it does not require a resale certificate of occupancy for a home sale. The Census Bureau estimates 69,105 residents for July 2025 across 46.17 square miles of land, or about 1,481 people per square mile at the 2020 count.

Housing figures for 2020-2024 show a 69.3% owner-occupied rate, a median home value of $457,900 and median gross rent of $2,115. Median household income is $124,648 and the mean commute to work is 33.5 minutes.

Nearly 35% of residents were born outside the United States, and 40.6% of people over five speak a language other than English at home.

How did the villages and history of Franklin Township shape its housing?

Franklin Township is a collection of villages that grew together over about 280 years. The area was organized around 1745 as the Eastern precinct, and the state recognized the township on February 21, 1798, among the first 104 townships in New Jersey.

The Delaware and Raritan Canal, built in the 1830s, drove early growth, and the old canal towpath is now a state park along the township's northern and western edges. Rockingham, near Kingston, is where George Washington wrote his farewell address to the army in 1783.

Today the named communities include Somerset, Franklin Park, East Franklin, Middlebush, Griggstown, Kingston, Six Mile Run, Pleasant Plains, East Millstone, Blackwells Mills and Weston. In the 2010 census Somerset counted 22,083 people and Franklin Park 13,295, which makes those two the largest. Buyers search by these village names, so use them in your listing or in your conversation with a cash buyer.

Does Franklin Township require a certificate of continued occupancy to sell a home?

No. The township's construction office states that a Certificate of Continued Occupancy inspection is not required when a residential home is sold in Franklin Township. What is required is an inspection from the Fire Prevention Department, reachable at 732-873-2500, extension 6303.

That fire inspection is the state's smoke alarm, carbon monoxide alarm and portable extinguisher compliance check, and the township posts a smoke alarm application among its forms. Commercial sales are different: the township requires a Certificate of Continued Building Compliance for a commercial building or when a new tenant takes the space.

What should a Franklin Township owner check about permits and historic districts?

Check two things: whether work on the house was permitted, and whether the property sits in a historic district. The township's permit instructions note that under the Uniform Construction Code, replacing roofs and siding on one- and two-family detached homes no longer requires a construction permit (polypropylene siding is the exception).

That relief does not apply in a historic district. All siding and roof replacements there still need Historic Commission review and approval before work starts, and the township publishes a map of the districts.

  • Look at your last roof, siding, deck and basement jobs and confirm the paperwork exists.
  • Check the township's district map if you plan any exterior repair before selling.
  • Call the Construction Department at 732-873-7283, extension 6224, when you are unsure whether a job needed a permit.

What does Franklin Township require for a vacant or foreclosure property?

The township regulates vacant and abandoned residential properties in foreclosure through Chapter 183 of its code, amended by Ordinance 4393-23, effective March 26, 2023. A mortgagee must inspect after filing a foreclosure complaint and register the property with the Township Clerk within 10 days, with a nonrefundable annual fee capped at $500.

The ordinance matters to a seller because it spells out what happens at transfer. Upon sale or transfer of a covered property, the owner is responsible for all code violations and must meet the Code Enforcement office within 45 days for a final courtesy inspection report. A failure to maintain a covered property can lead to a summons with a fine of up to $1,500.

If you own a house that is headed toward foreclosure, selling before a complaint is filed avoids this registration track altogether. Ask the Clerk's Office whether your address already appears on the vacant property register.

How does the reduced realty transfer fee for seniors apply in Franklin Township?

New Jersey charges a lower realty transfer fee when the seller is a senior citizen, blind or disabled. With Franklin Township's 18.3% share of residents aged 65 or older, this schedule applies to many local sales.

For a price of $350,000 or less, the reduced rates are $0.50 per $500 on the first $150,000 and $1.25 per $500 on the portion from $150,000 to $350,000. Above $350,000, the schedule starts at $1.40 per $500 and climbs to $2.65 per $500 for the slice between $550,000 and $850,000.

A seller claiming the reduced schedule files the RTF-1 affidavit with the deed in the Somerset County Clerk's office. Ask your closing attorney to confirm that the seller qualifies before you rely on the lower figure.

A separate GIT/REP residency form travels with the deed as well. The Division of Taxation says the person who signs the deed completes it, and a New Jersey resident uses the GIT/REP-3.

How do schools, highways and parks shape buyer interest in Franklin Township?

Buyers look first at the school district, then at Interstate 287, then at open space. Franklin Township Public Schools serve pre-K through grade 12 across 10 schools, with 7,352 students in 2023-24.

Interstate 287 crosses the northern part of the township with two interchanges, and county routes 514, 518 and 527 carry local traffic. The New Jersey Turnpike lies just outside the township, with its closest interchanges two towns away in Edison, East Brunswick and Monroe.

  • Colonial Park, a 685.5-acre Somerset County park, includes the Arboretum, a rose garden and a golf course.
  • Six Mile Run Reservoir Site, a 3,037-acre state parcel, offers multi-use trails.
  • The Ten Mile Run Greenway covers 684 acres and runs over four miles in length.

The municipality maintains 216.72 of roughly 260 road miles, while Somerset County keeps 34.67 and the state 8.73.

Which sale route fits a Franklin Township seller?

Because Franklin does not ask for a resale certificate of occupancy, the timeline is shorter than in towns that do. The fire inspection and the deed recording are the two fixed steps, and everything else depends on the buyer.

  • A traditional listing works well for a house in good condition when you can wait on a buyer's financing.
  • A private sale suits an owner who already has a buyer and an attorney.
  • A cash offer fits a house with deferred repairs, an estate or a foreclosure notice, as long as the fire inspection is scheduled early.

Call Fire Prevention first, then set the closing date with the buyer's attorney.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a resale certificate of occupancy in Franklin Township?

No. The township's construction office says a Certificate of Continued Occupancy is not required for a residential sale. You still need the Fire Prevention Department's smoke alarm, carbon monoxide alarm and extinguisher inspection.

Who inspects smoke and carbon monoxide alarms before a Franklin Township sale?

The Fire Prevention Department does. Its number is 732-873-2500, extension 6303, and the township posts a smoke alarm application among its fire prevention forms.

Can I replace my roof before selling without a permit in Franklin Township?

Usually yes for a one- or two-family detached home, since the Uniform Construction Code no longer mandates a permit for roof replacement. A house in a historic district is the exception: it needs Historic Commission approval first.

What is the senior citizen realty transfer fee in New Jersey?

It is a lower schedule for senior citizen, blind or disabled sellers. For prices up to $350,000 it is $0.50 per $500 on the first $150,000 and $1.25 per $500 on the portion up to $350,000, claimed on the RTF-1 affidavit.

What happens to a foreclosure property when it sells in Franklin Township?

The owner becomes responsible for all code violations at transfer and must meet the Code Enforcement office within 45 days for a courtesy inspection report. Mortgagees register covered properties with the Township Clerk within 10 days of their inspection.

How do you sell a house fast in Hillsborough, New Jersey?

A seller here has three practical paths: an agent's listing, a sale without an agent, or a buyer who pays cash and takes the house in its present condition. The township is in Somerset County, in the Raritan Valley, and its own website describes it as 52 miles from Manhattan.

Speed in Hillsborough depends less on the price you pick than on the paperwork. A smoke detector certificate, any open building permits and a clean tax record decide how soon a closing date can be set.

  • Agent listing: the widest exposure, but showings, a buyer's mortgage and a repair list all add weeks.
  • Without an agent: the commission stays with you, along with the pricing, the contract and the arrangements for the township's alarm inspection.
  • Cash buyer: no lender and no repair negotiation, so the timeline is mostly the title work and the certificate inspection.

Weigh each path by the dollars left after fees and repairs.

Where is Hillsborough and how did it develop?

Hillsborough Township covers 55.10 square miles, which makes it the largest of Somerset County's 21 municipalities by area. Its 54.61 square miles of land include several named communities, among them Belle Mead, Neshanic, Flagtown, Amwell and Woods Tavern.

A royal charter created the township in September 1771, and the Legislature incorporated it on February 21, 1798. Millstone split off as a borough in 1894 and Manville in 1929. Growth came mostly after 1950: the population went from 3,875 that year to 36,634 in 2000 and 43,276 in the 2020 census, according to the encyclopedia entry on the township.

Nearly 40 percent of the land is protected or preserved open space. That includes Duke Farms, a 2,700 acre estate in the northeast corner, so a house near preserved land will often have farm or woodland views that stay put.

The climate is humid subtropical. January lows average 18 degrees and July highs reach 85. Annual precipitation of 47.85 inches puts roofs, gutters and basements on a buyer's inspection list.

What do Census figures say about Hillsborough homes and owners?

Owners live in 79.5 percent of Hillsborough's housing units. An owned home has a median value of $547,600. At the median, owners carrying a mortgage spend $3,017 a month on housing and owners without one spend $1,470.

There are 16,388 households of about 2.67 people each, with median income of $154,031 and an average commute of 33.3 minutes. Turnover is low: 91.1 percent of residents were at the same address a year earlier. Population is estimated at 45,061 for July 2025, a 4.1 percent gain over the 2020 base.

For a seller this means your likely buyer is a commuter household with a sizable income, and a listing competes with a modest supply of similar homes. A buyer who needs cash certainty or no financing contingency is a smaller group but a real one.

Which roads, buses and schools do buyers weigh in Hillsborough?

Buyers here ask about the commute and the school district before they ask about the kitchen. The facts below come from the township's entry on the public encyclopedia.

  • Roads: U.S. Route 206 is the main route. A 3.75 mile bypass finished in 2021, and the old road is meant to become a downtown main street. County Routes 514 and 533 also cross the township, while Interstate 287 sits just outside in Bridgewater and Franklin.
  • Transit: D.H.I.L.A.N. buses link to Manville, Bridgewater and Somerville, and Coach USA runs four weekday morning express trips to Midtown Manhattan. A proposed West Trenton rail line with Belle Mead and Hillsborough stops was cancelled for lack of funding.
  • Schools: the Hillsborough Township School District runs pre-kindergarten through grade 12. Its nine schools include five K to 4 elementaries, Auten Road Intermediate for grades 5 and 6, a middle school for 7 and 8 and the high school. Enrollment was 7,288 in 2020-21.

What paperwork does a Hillsborough seller handle before closing?

Four offices touch a Hillsborough sale: the Fire Safety Department, the Building Department, the Tax Collector and the Somerset County Clerk. The table lists what each one asks of the seller.

Hillsborough closing checklist, from the township Building and Tax pages and the Somerset County Clerk land records page
ItemOfficeWhat to know
Smoke detector certificationFire Safety DepartmentFor a resale, the Building Department does not issue a certificate of occupancy. Schedule this inspection instead.
Open permitsBuilding DepartmentThe current owner must close any open permit, even one pulled by a previous owner.
Quarterly taxesTax CollectorBilled on the first of February, May, August and November. Payment is on time through the 10th.
Deed recordingSomerset County ClerkA county cover sheet goes with every deed. The first page costs $45 and each added page $10.

The township's SDL portal shows permit status and inspection results, so pull the permit history for your address early. Fixing a stale permit takes less time than explaining it to a buyer's attorney.

How are Hillsborough property taxes billed and what happens when you sell?

The township mails an estimated third-quarter bill each July, based on the current year's assessed value. The Tax Collector warns against multiplying that bill by four, because adjustments land in the third and fourth quarters.

Hillsborough runs an annual reassessment program, so assessments follow market movement from year to year. Township figures show the rate falling from $2.419 per $100 of assessed value in 2018 to $2.143 in 2024, even as values climbed. A check mailed on the 9th but received on the 12th is late, because the office ignores postmarks.

If you pay by ACH direct debit, tell the Tax Collector as soon as you list. The office says debits continue until it is notified. A seller with unpaid taxes should request a payoff figure ahead of closing. The township's online auction of 2025 and prior delinquent charges ran from August 21 to September 23, 2026.

Assessment appeals go to the Somerset County Board of Taxation. The statewide date is April 1, pushed to May 1 in a district that has been revalued or reassessed, so confirm which one fits your parcel. If the board rules against you, the Tax Court takes a petition for 45 days after the ruling.

What does the state add to the cost of selling in Hillsborough?

Recording the deed triggers New Jersey's Realty Transfer Fee, and the seller pays it. At the Hillsborough median value of $547,600 the schedule for sales above $350,000 applies, and the $4.80 per $500 band covers most of the price. The Division of Taxation publishes every band.

A seller who stays a New Jersey resident signs GIT/REP-3 at the table, so no income tax is estimated at closing. A home that was your main residence for two of the five years before sale may qualify for the gain exclusion that New Jersey follows: $250,000 for one filer, $500,000 for joint filers.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a certificate of occupancy to sell my Hillsborough house?

Not from the Building Department, which says it issues none for a residential resale. The Fire Safety Department handles a smoke detector certification inspection, and that is the visit you book. Your closing attorney can say whether a buyer's lender wants anything more.

When are Hillsborough property taxes due?

On the first of February, May, August and November. A grace period runs through the 10th and extends to the next business day when the 10th lands on a weekend or holiday. After that, interest is charged back to the first, and a postmark does not rescue a late payment.

What is the deadline to appeal a Hillsborough assessment?

Usually April 1, on Form A-1 with the Somerset County Board of Taxation. Where a revaluation or reassessment has been carried out the date shifts to May 1. The board or the township assessor can tell you which one governs your parcel before you prepare the petition.

Who records the deed when I sell in Hillsborough?

The Somerset County Clerk, whose office files deeds, mortgages and related papers. Every filing needs a county cover sheet, and e-recording runs through certified partners. Recording a deed costs $45 for page one and $10 for each page after, and your title company normally submits it.

Can I sell a Hillsborough house that has open permits or needs repairs?

Yes, though open permits stay attached to the house. Under the township's rule, whoever owns the property must close an open permit, even one a prior owner pulled. Cash buyers will take a house needing repairs, but resolving the permit first avoids a snag at closing.

How do you sell a house fast in Union, NJ?

The quickest sale in Union is a cash purchase by an investor or family buyer who accepts the property in its present state and orders the township's resale inspection. A listing suits a well kept house in a sought-after pocket, and selling without an agent is permitted, but a resale certificate is part of every route.

Union here means Union Township in Union County, not Union City in Hudson County. The Census Bureau counts 63,675 people in the township for mid-2025, up 6.6% from the 2020 estimates base of 59,733 and up from 56,642 at the 2010 Census. The township covers 9.05 square miles of land, a 2020 density of 6,599 people per square mile.

What is Union Township like, and where are its neighborhoods?

The township sits on the northern edge of Union County and borders eight municipalities: Hillside, Elizabeth, Roselle Park, Kenilworth and Springfield Township, plus Maplewood, Irvington and Millburn across the Essex County line. It was once called Connecticut Farms, was settled in 1667, and was incorporated as a township on November 23, 1808. It became part of Union County in 1857. The Battle of Connecticut Farms was fought here in June 1780.

Residents describe their location by neighborhood more than by the township name, and each pocket has its own character.

  • Five Points, around the junction of Galloping Hill Road, Chestnut Street and Salem Road.
  • Union Center, near Morris and Stuyvesant Avenues.
  • Vauxhall, north of Interstate 78, with its own ZIP code, 07088.
  • Putnam Manor and Putnam Ridge, an older residential section off Colonial Avenue and Morris Avenue.
  • Battle Hill, in the west near the Rahway River and Route 22, and Larchmont Estates by the Larchmont Reservation.
  • Green Lane, a newer community between Kean University and Union Station.

What do Union homes cost, and who owns them?

In the 2020 to 2024 survey period, Union's median owner-occupied value was $451,300, with 71.5% of the 21,374 households owning their home. Median gross rent is $2,064. Median household income is $119,464, about 41% of adults have a four-year degree, and 6.7% of residents live in poverty.

Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $3,015, and owners without one report $1,292. Owner-occupants are the large majority here, and homes range from the historic section of Putnam Manor to the poured-concrete houses on Ingersoll Terrace that Thomas Edison experimented with. About 37.1% of residents were born outside the United States.

What must a Union seller do before closing?

Union requires a Residential Resale Certificate, also called a certificate of continued occupancy, before a sale. The township's procedure sheet says requests must be made at least ten business days before the inspection date, and the certificate is not issued until the inspection fee is paid. The purpose of the visit is to verify smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and fire extinguishers, and every open permit must be closed with the proper inspections first.

Inspections run on weekdays from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., and the owner or a representative must be at the house during those hours or a second visit is scheduled at an added charge. The certificate is issued two full business days after final approval and stays valid for three months unless occupancy or ownership changes. It is not transferable.

What does a Union resale inspection look for?

The township's checklist is short and concrete, so a seller can prepare in a weekend.

  • At least one smoke detector on each level, plus one within 10 feet of each separate sleeping area. Two-family houses also need one at the top of each common stairwell.
  • Carbon monoxide alarms outside each sleeping area, within 10 feet of the bedroom doors.
  • A fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen, no smaller than 2A:10B:C and no larger than 10 pounds, mounted no more than five feet off the floor and in plain view.
  • Smoke alarms mounted to the manufacturer's directions with no double-sided tape, and the extinguisher on a hanger or bracket.
  • Existing hardwired detection systems from a newer build or renovation kept working, since battery units are not accepted as replacements.

Test every alarm before the inspector arrives. A failed visit means another $80 and another wait, and a cash buyer will often fix these small items before closing so the certificate can issue.

How long does the Union resale process take?

Plan on at least two to three weeks from request to certificate. The township wants ten business days of notice before the inspection, and the certificate comes two full business days after final approval. If the first visit fails, the housing inspector books a second one, which adds the $80 fee and another wait.

Because the certificate lasts three months, a seller can apply as soon as a contract is signed without much risk of it lapsing before closing. When the buyer wants a quick closing, apply the day the contract is signed. Ask the township whether any permits on the house, such as a finished basement or a deck, are still open, since the inspection cannot pass until they are closed.

How does Union bill property taxes?

Union property taxes are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a 10-day grace period. The state does not accept postmarks as proof of payment, so a payment must be physically in the Tax Office by 4:30 p.m. to be credited that day. A drop box at the front door of the municipal building on Morris Avenue works around the clock, and cash should never go in it.

The Tax Office collects municipal, county and school taxes and sewer utility bills. Bills equal assessed value times the tax rate, and the Union County Board of Taxation certifies the rate. The collector cannot lower a tax or waive interest. Ask the Tax Office for the quarter-by-quarter status before closing so the title company can prorate correctly. For relief programs, the township's tax page links to a property tax relief page.

How do roads, rail and Kean University affect Union buyers?

Union has about 145.85 miles of roads, crossed by the Garden State Parkway, Interstate 78, U.S. Route 22 and Route 82 on Morris Avenue. Parkway interchanges 139A, 139B, 140, 140A and 141 serve the township. The Union station on NJ Transit's Raritan Valley Line runs to Newark Penn Station, and its lot holds over 450 cars. Bus routes 113, 114 and 117 go to the Port Authority Bus Terminal in Midtown Manhattan, and Newark Liberty International Airport is about six miles east.

Kean University moved to the township in 1958 and serves almost 16,000 students. The Union Public School District runs six PreK-4 elementary schools, Jefferson School for fifth grade, Burnet and Kawameeh middle schools, and Union High School, which enrolled 2,270 students in 2021-22. Retail is a major local strength: the Census Bureau reports 2022 retail sales of $2,699,105,000, or $44,579 per resident, and the township has a 217,000-square-foot Home Depot that was the chain's largest store as of 2012.

Frequently asked questions

Is a resale certificate mandatory in Union, NJ?

Yes, the township requires a Residential Resale Certificate of continued occupancy before a sale. The inspection costs $175 and must be requested at least ten business days ahead.

How long does the Union resale certificate last?

It stays valid for three months from issue unless occupancy or ownership changes in the meantime. It cannot be transferred to another property or owner.

What does the Union inspector check?

The visit checks smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and fire extinguishers, and confirms that every open permit has been closed. Test the alarms before the inspector arrives.

What if my Union house fails the resale inspection?

A re-inspection costs $80, and the seller calls the housing inspector for a new appointment instead of reapplying. Fix the listed items first, since each extra visit adds cost and delay.

What are the Union tax due dates?

Bills fall due each February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, followed by a 10-day grace period, and postmarks earn no credit. Payments must be in the Tax Office by 4:30 p.m. to count that day.
